title: Team Permissions Playground — UX notes & grooming
body:
Purpose:
This is a working UX doc for the "Team Permissions Playground" — a compact, discoverable console surface where org admins and platform engineers can manage RBAC, API keys, service accounts, and audit log views. Goal is to reduce cognitive load when performing common tasks (create role, issue scoped key, inspect service account usage, investigate an audit event) while keeping advanced controls available.

Background / context:
- We currently surface RBAC across two disconnected places: legacy org settings and the new dedicated roles API. Admins report friction when searching for a role, creating scoped API keys, and correlating keys with service accounts in audit trails.
- Scope here covers console UX (not backend policy engine). Wireframes will inform a one-screen MVP and a progressive disclosure design for advanced settings.

Primary personas:
- Org Admin (safety-first, audits, needs clear trails)
- Platform Engineer (automation, service accounts, keys for CI)
- App Developer (requests role changes, needs short-lived keys)

Success metrics (tracked via console events):
- Reduction in average time-to-issue-key for platform engineers from ~6m to <3m.
- Decrease in support tickets about "cannot find role" by 40% in Q1 after launch.
- 75% of new keys created using scoped templates (less privilege)

High-level UX requirements:
- Single top-level nav: "Teams & Access" (not buried in Settings).
- Quick filter: search roles, users, service accounts, API keys in one go.
- Role editor with sample permissions preview and "what this lets them do" copy.
- API key creation as a guided flow: select owner (user vs service account), scope template (read-only/embed/generate), expiry, and explicit confirmation showing impact.
- Service account creation flow with optional key rotation schedule and linked deployment notes.
- Audit log quick-inspect: ability to filter to events related to an API key / service account / role and to jump to the role or key page.

Wireframe notes (visual layout described):
Top-level screen (Teams & Access) — three-column layout for desktop:
- Left column (nav + quick-create): static list of org units -> team selector; quick action buttons: Create Role, New API Key, New Service Account, Open Audit.
- Middle column (master list): combined search bar above a tabbed list (Roles | Users | Service Accounts | API Keys). Search supports syntax: "type:service-account owner:infra expires:<7d"
- Right column (detail panel): slide-over for item detail. When creating new item, this becomes the guided flow.

Role detail / editor:
- Top: role name, human short description, sample principle (e.g., "For deployment pipelines")
- Middle: permission checklist grouped by surface (Console, API, Embeds, Billing) with toggles and an immediate natural-language preview: "This role can: read model catalog, launch dedicated instances, not view billing."
- Bottom: sample resource safe-listing (optional) to restrict to team-owned models / projects.
- Versioning: show last changed by + time + diff link to last policy change.
- Acceptance criteria: role saves as idempotent; preview text must be readable at glance; changes produce an audit entry.

API key creation flow (guided):
Step 1: Owner selection: radio: User | Service account. If service account, quick link to create SA.
Step 2: Scope: templates + custom mode. Each template shows example allowed endpoints and a token TTL suggestion.
Step 3: TTL & rotation: quick presets (1h, 1d, 7d, 30d, custom) with inline note: "shorter TTLs reduce blast radius".
Step 4: Bindings: optional resource-restriction (model ids, domain, IP ranges). If custom binding is selected, show validation for CIDR and model ids.
Step 5: Confirm + copy secret. Show an admonition: "This key will only be shown once." Provide a downloadable JSON with metadata (key id, owner, expires_at, scope).
Edge cases: if org policy requires KMS-wrapped keys, disable secret copy and route to key-creation request flow (RINF-2167).

Service account page:
- Show linked deployments (quick sniff: Kubernetes ServiceAccountName, cloud function ident) or manual annotations.
- Rotation schedule UI: inline calendar for rotation cadence + one-click rotate now.
- Allow attaching a team and default role templates for keys created by this SA.
- Acceptance criteria: adding an annotation must be write-audited; rotate action should create an audit entry and optionally generate a new key.

Audit log view (focused mode):
- Default list: chronologic with compact cards showing event type, actor, target, time, and quick action icons (Jump to Role / Jump to Key / Revoke Key).
- Filters: actor (user/service account), resource (role/key/service-account), event-type (create/update/revoke/login), date range.
- Correlation helper: when viewing a key-related event, show the last 5 events for that key and the role-binding at event time.
- Export: CSV export with columns (timestamp, actor, target, action, ip, user-agent, request-id).

Mobile considerations:
- Use a single-column stack. Prioritize actions: Search at top, master list as primary, detail slide-in.
- Copy secret step should warn mobile users and offer to email the key (org policy permitting).

Accessibility / copy notes:
- Use clear verbs: "Issue key" vs "Create token" to avoid confusion with login tokens.
- Provide aria-labels for quick actions and ensure keyboard-first flows for role editing.

Backlog (groomed tasks — prioritized):
1) R1 (P0) — Combined Search + master list tabs + slide-over detail (3 SP)
   - Acceptance: search supports type filters; clicking item opens slide-over; analytics event on open.
2) R2 (P0) — API Key guided creation flow (5 SP)
   - Acceptance: create key endpoint called, secret returned once, UI shows success and download link.
3) R3 (P1) — Role editor with permission preview and save/diff (4 SP)
   - Acceptance: permission toggles persist, preview updates synchronously.
4) R4 (P1) — Service account page + rotation (3 SP)
   - Acceptance: create SA, attach annotation, rotate key creates new key obj + audit log.
5) R5 (P1) — Audit log focused mode + correlation panel (4 SP)
   - Acceptance: filter by key/SA/role and show correlated events inline.
6) R6 (P2) — Policy-required KMS flow + blocked secret copy (2 SP)
   - Dependency: backend feature RINF-2167.
7) R7 (P2) — Mobile layout adjustments & email-key flow (2 SP)

Implementation notes / dependencies:
- Backend: require key creation API to return metadata and one-time secret. If org KMS policy exists, behavior changes; coordinate with security (RINF-2167).
- Telemetry: instrument search queries, create-key events (with anonymized scope), rotation events.
- Security: prevent copy if org policy, rate-limit create-key endpoint for service accounts.

Open questions / decision points:
- Should role templates (e.g., "embed-only", "billing-read") be writable by org admins or only product? Proposal: allow org admins to clone and edit templates; product-provided templates are read-only.
- Do we show permission-level diffs inline for large roles? If a role has >100 flags, show summarized bullets + "show full JSON".
- Audit retention: default retention for UI export should be 90 days; deeper retention via export or premium plan. Need legal sign-off.

Copy snippets (for UI):
- Create API key: "Issue API key — choose owner, scope, expiry. This secret will be shown once."
- Role preview: "This role can: read model catalog, list deployments, create inference jobs (no billing)."
- Audit event card: "John K. created API key key-4b2f — 2026-02-14 09:12 UTC"

Next steps / owners:
- Design: produce high-fidelity frames for the 3-col desktop layout and mobile stack (Lena Park) — due 2026-03-02.
- Backend: align create-key behavior and KMS gating with Security (Samir) — dependency check by 2026-02-28.
- Product: finalize prioritization for Q2 scope (Aisha) — decision meeting 2026-02-24.

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally informal: focus on flows and acceptance criteria. Flag any regulatory or policy constraints early (legal/security).
- If you see any UX anti-patterns (e.g., burying revoke key behind 3 clicks), call them out in comments here and link to a Jira spike if needed.

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12 initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2025-11-05 added API key TTL presets + templates (Marco)
- 2026-01-18 audit correlation ideas added (Joan)
- 2026-02-20 grooming pass, prioritized backlog and acceptance criteria (Lena)
